lines.text: What did you just sign? Bartholomew Roberts' rules.
The man giving orders isn't the captain. It's the quartermaster, chosen by the crew.
A book printed in 1724 says any man could walk in and help himself to the captain's dinner.
That accent comes from films made in the 1950s.
On Howell Davis's ship, where Roberts learned the trade, the rules promised the best pair of pistols on board.
The same book quotes Blackbeard's own journal.
Strike another man on board, and the same ship gave you what they called Moses's Law.
Pirates often flew false colours, a friendly flag, so their target would let them come close.
That's exactly how it ended for Roberts' crew, in 1722.
